title: Mulayam Singh v. U.P. Power Corporation, Lucknow
coram: Amreshwar Pratap Sahi, J.; Rajiv Lochan Mehrotra, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; petitioner relegated to clauses 6.5, 7.10 and 6.14.
headnote: Electricity billing disputes are to be decided by the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. A consumer aggrieved by that decision may file an appeal or approach the Consumer Grievances Redressal Forum under clause 7.10. If quantum is not disputed and the consumer proposes to deposit, instalments may be sought from the Executive Engineer under clause 6.14. A third writ on the same arrears was disposed of by directing those remedies.
facts: Mulayam Singh challenged recovery of Rs 1,18,860 of electricity arrears, referred by the Executive Engineer, Etah Division, to the Collector. Writ-C No. 1896 of 2017 was dismissed on 16 January 2017 because he had not approached departmental officers. After he represented on 23 January 2017, Writ-C No. 13844 of 2017 directed the Executive Engineer to decide that representation within three weeks. This third petition again assailed the same billing. He disputed the factum of consumption and the bill.

holding_units.holding: All billing disputes are to be decided by the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If the consumer is aggrieved, an appeal may be filed or the Consumer Grievances Redressal Forum approached under clause 7.10. Where the factum of consumption and billing is disputed, those remedies are to be availed. If the consumer does not dispute the quantum and proposes to deposit the amount, the Executive Engineer may be approached for instalments under clause 6.14.

not_decided.point: Whether the Rs 1,18,860 arrears and the factum of consumption were correctly billed
not_decided.note: Merits of the billing dispute left to the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 and, if needed, clause 7.10.
